statements.claim: Arjuna had just won victory over the son of Drona and searched his own troops because Yudhishthira was gone from the field
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'Having vanquished the son of Drona... Dhananjaya... cast his eyes among his own troops... Not seeing his brother Yudhishthira...'

statements.claim: Bhima told Arjuna the king had left the field, his limbs scorched by Karna's shafts, and whether he still lived was doubtful
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: Bhima said, 'King Yudhishthira the just, hath gone away from this place, his limbs scorched with Karna's shafts. It is doubtful whether he still liveth!'

statements.claim: Arjuna recalled that the king had stayed in battle, pierced by Drona's arrows, expectant of victory, until Drona was slain
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'though deeply pierced by Drona with keen shafts, the king... had still stayed in battle, expectant of victory, until Drona was slain!'

statements.claim: Arjuna judged the king had gone to the camp and asked Bhima to go for news while he stayed to check the foes
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'Without doubt... the king hath gone to the camp!... quickly go hence, O Bhima! I will stay here, checking all our foes!'

statements.claim: Bhima refused to go, saying heroes would call him frightened in battle, and offered to fight all the samsaptakas himself so Arjuna could go
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'If, O Arjuna, I go there, many foremost of heroes will then say that I am frightened in battle!'... 'I will fight with all the samsaptakas in battle! Therefore, O Dhananjaya, do thou go thyself!'

statements.claim: Arjuna asked Krishna to urge the steeds and leave the sea of troops so he could see king Ajatasatru
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'Urge the steeds, O Hrishikesha, leaving this sea of troops! I desire, O Keshava to see king Ajatasatru!'

statements.claim: Krishna told Bhima the feat was not wonderful for him and bade him slay the assembled foes of Partha
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'This feat is not at all wonderful for thee, O Bhima! I am about to go (hence). Slay these assembled foes of Partha!'

statements.claim: Krishna drove at great speed on Garuda-like steeds to where the king lay alone on his bed; both alighted and worshipped Yudhishthira's feet
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'Then Hrishikesha proceeded with very great speed to the spot where king Yudhishthira was... borne by those steeds that resembled Garuda... approached the king who was lying alone on his bed. Both of them, alighting from that car, worshipped the feet of king Yudhishthira the just.'

statements.claim: Seeing the king safe, the two were filled with joy, and the king, thinking Karna had been slain, spoke with voice choked with delight
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'the two Krishnas became filled with joy... King Yudhishthira the just, thinking that Karna had been slain, became filled with joy... addressed them in these words in a voice choked with delight.'

statements.claim: 'He was wrong' - the king's belief that Karna had fallen (narrator's comment closing the scene)
statements.evidence: The joy was based on a mistaken belief ('thinking that Karna had been slain'); corpus chain next story has the duel with Karna continuing, so Karna was not slain at this point.

notes: Close, nearly verbatim rendering of MBh 8.65 dialogue and action; only the 'he was wrong' coda is editorial commentary, factually consistent with the continuing duel.

statements.claim: Arjuna and Karna, both owning white steeds, met in combat like two infuriated elephants fighting for a she-elephant
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'those two foremost of men, both owning white steeds... closed with each other like two infuriated Himalayan elephants, both of full-grown tusks, fighting... for the sake of a she-elephant in her season.'

statements.claim: They poured showers of arrows like clouds meeting clouds or mountain meeting mountain, with twanging bows and clattering car-wheels, while both armies watched
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'Like a mass of clouds encountering another mass, or a mountain encountering a mountain, those two warriors, both pouring showers of arrows, encountered each other, their bows loudly twanging... and the wheels of their cars producing a deafening clatter.' Armies/welkin struck with fear: same passage.

statements.claim: Karna first pierced Arjuna with ten shafts; Arjuna pierced him in return with ten shafts in the centre of the chest
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'Then Karna first pierced Partha in that encounter, with ten mighty shafts. Arjuna pierced him in return with ten keen-pointed shafts... in the centre of the chest.'

statements.claim: Limbs of the heroes, drivers and horses were mangled and blood flowed like a river whose water none would drink
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'marked by a river whose distasteful water consisted of blood, the limbs of those two heroes, as also their drivers and animals, became exceedingly mangled.'

statements.claim: Arjuna rubbed his arms and Gandiva's string and sped cloth-yard shafts, nalikas, boar's-ear-headed arrows, razors, anjalikas and crescent arrows, all cut off by Karna
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'Rubbing his two arms and the string also of Gandiva... Arjuna, then sped showers of cloth-yard shafts, and Nalikas and arrows equipped with heads like boar's ears and razors, and Anjalikas, and crescent-shaped arrows... all those successive showers... were cut off by the Suta's son.'

statements.claim: Spectators raised leonine shouts and waved fingers and cloths when Arjuna rushed against Karna
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'Others among the spectators, filled with joy and uttering leonine shouts, raised their arms, waving their fingers or the pieces of cloth they held, when Arjuna rushed against the son of Adhiratha.'

statements.claim: Arjuna loosed a fiery weapon covering earth, welkin and compass points and hiding the sun; warriors' robes caught fire and they fled
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'The son of Indra then sped at Karna a fiery weapon... Covering the earth and the welkin and the ten points of the compass and the very course of the sun... The robes of all the warriors took fire, at which they fled away.'

statements.claim: Karna quenched the conflagration with the varunastra - clouds dark as mountains flooded the field and the fire was quenched in a trice
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'the Suta's son Karna... shot... the varunastra for quenching it... Those clouds whose extremities presented the aspect of mountains, surrounding every side, flooded the earth with water. That fierce conflagration... was still quenched by those clouds in a trice.'

statements.claim: The Somakas urged Arjuna to pierce Karna and cut off his head; the Kauravas urged Karna to slay Arjuna and send the sons of Pritha to the woods forever
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'The Somakas then loudly shouted to Partha... pierce Karna. Cut off his head...' and Karna's side: 'slay Arjuna with keen shafts. Let the sons of Pritha once more go to the woods forever.'

statements.claim: Krishna rebuked Arjuna for letting Karna crush his weapons and offered him the razor-edged Sudarsana to strike off Karna's head, like Sakra slaying Namuci with the thunderbolt
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt from MBh 8.89: 'Then Vasudeva, beholding Partha's shafts baffled by Karna, said... What is this, O diadem-decked Arjuna, that Karna should succeed in crushing thy weapons today... strike off the head of that foe of thine with this Sudarsana, of edge keen as a razor, that I give unto thee, like Sakra striking off the head of his foe Namuci, with the thunderbolt.'

notes: Story mirrors MBh 8.89 closely; pack passage truncates after the varunastra quench, but the Sudarsana offer is verbatim in the pack excerpt. Closing line is narrative pause, not a factual claim.

statements.claim: The broken Kaurava divisions fled before Arjuna's arrows and watched from a distance his weapon careering with the effulgence of lightning
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'Flying away in consequence of the falling of Arjuna's arrows, the broken divisions of the Kauravas, staying at a distance, continued to gaze at Arjuna's weapon... careering around with the effulgence of lightning.'

statements.claim: Karna crushed Arjuna's burning weapon with his foe-killing weapon received from Rama, resembling an Atharvan rite
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'the Suta's son now crushed [that weapon] with his shafts winged with gold... destroyed that burning weapon of Arjuna with his own foe-killing weapon of great power which he had obtained from Rama, and which resembled (in efficacy) an Atharvan rite.'

statements.claim: Scorched and mangled, unable to prevail, Karna reached for a single shaft that lay alone in his quiver, and did not know that the snake Aswasena had entered it
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'When at last Karna found that he could not prevail over Partha... set his heart upon that shaft of his which lay singly within a quiver.' Full text of same section: 'The Suta's son did not know that the snake Aswasena had entered his arrow by the aid of his Yoga powers.'

statements.claim: Aswasena, whose mother Arjuna slew at Khandava, had hidden in the nether region and now rose, took arrow form and entered Karna's quiver
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'the snake Aswasena, who was hostile to Arjuna, was passing his time in the nether region... recollecting the death of his mother... he quickly entered into Karna's quiver... in the form of an arrow.'

statements.claim: The shaft was snake-mouthed, blazing, polished according to rule, long kept for Partha's destruction, in a golden quiver amid sandal dust; Karna aimed it at Phalguna's head
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'that foe-killing, exceedingly keen, snake-mouthed, blazing, and fierce shaft... long kept for the sake of Partha's destruction... within a golden quiver amid sandal dust... aimed it at Partha... for cutting off Phalguna's head in battle.'

statements.claim: When the snake-arrow was fixed on the string, the Regents of the world including Sakra set up loud wails
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'When that snake of the form of an arrow was fixed on the bow-string, the Regents of the world, including Sakra, set up loud wails.'

statements.claim: Fatigued, the two heroes were fanned by apsaras with palm-leaf fans sprinkled with sandal-water while Sakra and Surya brushed their faces
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'those two heroes, fatigued with their exertions in battle, looked at each other. Both of them were then fanned with excellent and waving fans made of young (palm) leaves... by many Apsaras... And Sakra and Surya, using their hands, gently brushed the faces of those two heroes.'

statements.claim: The chariot stood sunk in the earth, where Krishna had pressed it down in the moment the arrow flew
statements.evidence: Full text of MBh 8.90 (same source chapter; pack passage truncated just before this scene): 'Madhava, with great speed... pressed down with his feet that excellent car, causing it to sink about a cubit deep.' Pack excerpt confirms the car was in the earth and Krishna raised it afterwards.

statements.claim: Krishna explained to Arjuna the snake's Khandava origin and told him to slay it; Arjuna cut the snake down
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90 pack excerpt: 'Whilst thou, armed with bow, wert engaged at Khandava in gratifying the god Agni, this snake was then in the sky, his body ensconced within his mother's... Remembering that act of hostility done by thee, he cometh towards thee today for thy destruction.' Full text: Krishna said 'Slay that great snake inimical to thee' and 'Jishnu... cut off, with six keen shafts, that snake in the welkin.'

statements.claim: After the snake was cut off, Krishna himself raised the car from the earth with his arms
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90 pack excerpt: 'After that snake had been cut off by Arjuna, the lord Keshava himself... raised up with his arms that car from the earth.'

statements.claim: Karna was left wounded and failing and the duel was not over
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90 continues with the duel: after raising the car, Karna pierced Krishna with ten shafts and the exchange resumed; corpus chain next story: 'Krishna Urges Arjuna to Slay the Distressed Karna.'

notes: Pack passage is truncated mid-chapter (ends at the Regents' wails); the chariot-pressing and slaying details were verified against the full Ganguli text of the same section 8.90, which the pack cites. Story omits the diadem-striking episode but asserts nothing contradicting it.

statements.claim: News of the war of the Kurus and Pandavas and the slaughter of the warrior kings reached Balarama from the mouths of brahmins, and he deemed the earth's burden lifted
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.21-22 (pack): 'Hearing of the battle of the Kurus and Pandavas and the slaughter of the warrior kings, Balarama, deeming the earth's burden lifted, goes to the field where Bhima and Duryodhana are fighting with maces.' Sanskrit v.21: 'srutva dvijaih kathyamanam kuru-pandava-samyuge.'

statements.claim: Balarama went to Kurukshetra where Bhima and Duryodhana were locked in their mace-duel, to stop it
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.22-23: Balarama goes to where Bhima and Duryodhana fight with maces; Vedabase 10.79.23: 'Wanting to stop the club fight then raging... Lord Balarama went to Kurukshetra.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira, the twins, Krishna and Arjuna went to greet Balarama when they saw him coming
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.23 (Sanskrit): 'yudhisthiras tu tam drstva yamau krsnariunav api.'

statements.claim: Balarama told the two equal champions - addressing the king and Vrikodara - that neither could win and bade them desist
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.25-26: 'yuvaam tulya-balau virau he rajan he vrikodara / tasmad ekatarasyeha yuvayoh sama-viryayoh'; pack excerpt: 'He tells the equal champions that neither can win and to desist.'

statements.claim: The two, bound by enmity and remembering mutual insults, did not heed his words
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.27: 'na tad-vakyam jagrihatur baddha-vairau nrparthavat'; pack excerpt: 'the two, bound by enmity and remembering mutual insults, do not heed his words.'

statements.claim: Accepting it as destiny, unable to part them, Balarama turned away and returned to Dwaraka
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.28: 'distam tad anumanvano ramo dvaravatim yayau' ('accepting that as destiny, Rama went to Dvaravati'); pack excerpt: 'Balarama, accepting it as destiny, returns to Dwaraka.'

statements.claim: He came from Dwaraka (as his point of departure for Kurukshetra)
statements.evidence: No support in the pack; SB 10.79.1-22 places Balarama on a pilgrimage tour of holy places (from Naimisharanya through southern India to Prabhasa) when he heard the brahmins' news and went to Kurukshetra; the text has him return TO Dvaraka after the duel (v.28), not set out from it.

corrections.original_sentence: He came from Dwaraka, and as he rode, the news was still turning in his mind — the war done, the kings fallen, and two champions yet beating each other to death.
corrections.suggested: He had been journeying through the holy places when the news reached him, and as he rode, the news was still turning in his mind — the war done, the kings fallen, and two champions yet beating each other to death.

notes: One unsupported detail: the story has Balarama set out from Dwaraka, but SB 10.79 (the pack's source) has him hear the news mid-pilgrimage and go to Kurukshetra from there, returning to Dvaravati afterwards. Rest of the story tracks the pack closely.

statements.claim: Freed from the brahma weapon of Ashvatthama, Kunti addressed Krishna as he turned to depart
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.16-17 (pack): 'Freed from the brahma weapon, Kunti addressed Krishna as he turned to depart.' Sanskrit v.16: 'brahma-tejo-vinirmuktair atmajaih saha krsnaya.'

statements.claim: She bowed to the primal Person, veiled by his own play, unknowable to the ignorant, imperishable, the goal of the pure-hearted sages
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.18-19: 'mayajavanikacchannam ajnadhyaksajam avyayam / ... paramahamsanam muninam amalatmanam.'

statements.claim: She bowed to Krishna son of Vasudeva and Devaki, lotus-navelled, garlanded with lotuses
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.20: 'krsnaya vasudevaya devaki-nandanaya ca / namah pankajanabhaya namah pankajamaline.'

statements.claim: She remembered Devaki shut up for a very long time in Kamsa's prison, given over to sorrow
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.22: 'yatha hrsikesa khalena devaki kamsena ruddhaticiram sucarpita.'

statements.claim: She recalled that he freed her and her children again and again from poison, the great fire, the cruel assembly of the dice hall, the hardships of forest exile and the weapons of mighty warriors
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.23 and pack summary: 'from poison, from the great fire, from the cruel assembly, from the hardships of forest exile, from the weapons of great chariot-warriors'; v.23: 'visan mahagneh purusadadarsanad asatsabhaya vanavasakrcchratah.'

statements.claim: 'May those dangers remain with me forever, teacher of the world, for it was in danger that I saw you' - a man puffed up by birth, wealth, learning and beauty does not see him
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.24-25: 'vipadah santu tah sasvat tatra tatra jagad-guro' and 'janmaisvarya-sruta-sribhir edhamana-madah puman.'

statements.claim: She called him the wealth of those who own nothing, beyond the world's moods, and considered him Time itself, lord without beginning and end; no one can read his intention as he moves in the guise of a man
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.26-28: 'namo 'kincana-vittaya nivrtta-guna-vrttaye / manye tvam kalam isanam anadi-nidhanam vibhum / na veda kascid bhagavams cikirsitam tavehamanasya nrinam vidambanam.'

statements.claim: Even the rope with which a gopi of Vrindavan bound him as a child, eyes blurred with tears and running collyrium, was his play
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.30: 'gopy adade tvayi krtagasi dama tavad ya te dasasru-kalilanjana-sambhramaksam.'

statements.claim: Some said the unborn one was born to give glory to the virtuous, others that Vasudeva prayed for him to come to Devaki, others that he came to lift the earth's burden like a boat on the ocean
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.31-33: 'kecid ahur ajam jatam punya-slokasya kirtaye / apare vasudevasya devakyam yacito 'bhyagat / bharavatarayanvanye bhuvo nava ivodadhau.'

statements.claim: 'Will you abandon us today...? What are we, Pandavas and Yadavas alike, without you, but name and form? This land will not shine as it shines now, bearer of the mace' - she named him Shri Krishna, friend of Arjuna, bull of the Vrishnis, of unending valor
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.36-38, 42: 'apy adya nas tvam... jihasasi svit suhrdo 'nujivinah / ke vayam nama-rupabhyam yadubhih saha pandavah / neyam sobhisyate tatra yathedanim gadadhara' and 'srikrsna krsna-sakha vrsny-rsabhavani-dhrug rajanya-vamsa-dahananapavarga-virya.'

statements.claim: She asked only that her mind be fixed on him alone, lord of Madhu, again and again
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.40-41: 'tvayi me 'nanya-visaya matir madhu-pate 'sakrt.'

statements.claim: Krishna, whose every glory she had praised, smiled gently and answered 'So be it', then turned back toward the city
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.44: 'tam badham ity upamantrya pravisya gajasahvayam' ('assuring her, 'So be it,' he entered Hastinapura'); pack excerpt: 'And the Lord, whose every glory she had praised, smiled gently.'

notes: The hymn's content maps verse-by-verse onto SB 1.8.16-44. The departure frame ('as Krishna prepares to leave Hastinapura for Dwaraka') matches the pack summary; Krishna re-entering the city at the close matches SB 1.8.44 and sets up the next story (SB 1.10 departure).

statements.claim: Krishna stayed in Hastinapura several months after the war, to gladden his friends and comfort his sister
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.6-7 (pack excerpt): 'Having stayed in Hastinapura some months to gladden his friends and please his sister, Hari took his leave, embraced and bowed to all, and mounted his chariot.'

statements.claim: Subhadra, Draupadi, Kunti, Gandhari and Dhritarashtra could not bear the separation, their eyes fixed on him as he departed
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.8, 12 (pack): 'Subhadra, Draupadi, Kunti, Gandhari, Dhritarashtra and the others could not bear the separation, their eyes fixed on him as he departed'; v.12: 'sarve te 'nimesair aksais tam anu druta-cetasah.'

statements.claim: The wise who have tasted true company cannot give it up; the Pandavas, whose minds were fixed on Krishna, could not endure his absence
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.10-11: 'satsangan mukta-duhsango hatum notsahate budhah / tasmin nyasta-dhiyah parthah saheran viraham katham.'

statements.claim: Tears rose in their eyes and were held back from longing for Devaki's son
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.13: 'nyarundhann udgalad-baspam autkanthyad devaki-sute.'

statements.claim: Mridangas, conches, bheris and vinas sounded; Kuru women climbed to the palace roofs to see him
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.14-15: 'mrdanga-sankha-bheryas ca vina-panava-gomukhah' and 'prasada-sikhararudhah kuru-naryo didrksaya.'

statements.claim: A white umbrella adorned with pearl garlands was held over him, Uddhava and Satyaki waved chauris, and brahmins' blessings were heard along the way
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.16-18: 'sitatapatram jagraha mukta-dama-vibhusitam / uddhavah satyakis caiva vijane paramadbhute / asruyantasisah satyas tatra tatra dvijeritah.'

statements.claim: The people spoke of him as the ancient Person who alone existed before all distinctions, who sets creation turning, whose feet sages seek, whose deeds are sung in the hidden Vedas, who descends when kings grow unrighteous
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.20-24: 'sa vai kilayam purusah puratano ya eka asid avisesa atmani... sa vayam yat padam atra surayo jitendriya... vedeSu guhyesu ca guhya-vadibhih... yada hy adharmena tamo-dhiyo nrpa jivanti tatraisa hi sattvatah kila.'

statements.claim: The women praised the clan of Yadu, the forest of Madhu, and Kushasthali which dims heaven's glory; the women won by valor at the svayamvara after defeating the fierce Chedi king make womanhood glorious
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.25-29: 'aho alam slaghya-tamam yadoh kulam... madhor vanam... kusasthali punya-yasaskari bhuva... ya virya-sulkena hrtah svayamvare pramathya caidya-pramukhan hi susminah... etah param stritvam... sadhu kurvate.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira rode with him part of the way to protect the army and escort; at the edge of the city the Kurus stood at a distance, tormented by separation
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.31-32: 'ajata-satruh prtanam gopithaya madhu-dvisah / atha duragatan saurih kauravan virahaturan.'

statements.claim: He travelled through Kuru-jangala, Panchala, Shurasena, the lands along the Yamuna, across the Maru desert, through the far reaches of Sauvira and Abhira, honored at every kingdom he crossed
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.33-35: 'kuru-jangala-pancalan surasenan sa-yamunan / maru-dhanvam atikramya sauvirabhira-yoh paran / tatra tatra ha tatratyair harih pratyudyat-arhanah.'

notes: Rendering of SB 1.10.6-35 is close and verse-faithful. Minor details (city children running beside the wheels; 'dead of two houses') are connective color that the source neither asserts nor contradicts.

statements.claim: Crossing into his own prosperous realm of Anarta, Krishna blew his conch, white-bellied and reddened by his lips, and the sound removes the fear of the world
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.1-2 and pack summary: 'Approaching his own prosperous land of Anarta, Krishna blew his conch to dispel his people's sorrow'; v.1-2: 'sa uccakase dhavalodaro daro 'py urukramasyadhara-sona-sonimah' and 'tam upasrutya ninadam jagad-bhaya-bhayavaham.'

statements.claim: Hearing it, the citizens rushed out to see their lord, faces blooming with joy, voices choked with delight
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.3-4: 'tatropanita-balayo raver dipam ivadrtah / prity-utphulla-mukhah procur harsa-gadgadaya gira.'

statements.claim: 'We bow to your lotus feet, worshipped by Brahma, Shiva and the kings of the gods... you alone are our mother, our friend, our husband, our father'
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.5-6: 'natah sma te natha sadanghri-pankajam virinca-vairincya-surendra-vanditam / bhavaya nas tvam bhava visva-bhavana tvam eva mata tha suhrt-pati-pita.'

statements.claim: 'When you went away to the Kurus or the Madhus to see your friends, how could we live... your glance dries up every sorrow'
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.8-9: 'yarhy ambujaksa apasasara bho bhavan kurun madhun vatha suhrd-didrksaya / katham vayam natha cirosite tvayi prasanna-drstya-khila-tapa-sosanam.'

statements.claim: Krishna, tender to his devotees, heard them all
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.10: 'iti codirita vacah prajanam bhaktavatsalah.'

statements.claim: The city was decked with arches at gates and along the roads, avenues swept, lanes, markets and squares freshened; at every door were pots of curds, unbroken rice, fruits and sugarcane
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.12-15: 'gopura-dvara-margesu krta-kautuka-toranam / sammarjita-mahamarga rathya-pana-katvaram / dvari dvari grhanam ca dadhy-aksata-phaleksubhih.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva, Akrura, Ugrasena, Balarama, and Pradyumna, Charudeshna and Samba (Jambavati's son) came out to meet him
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.16-17 and pack excerpt: 'Vasudeva, Akrura, Ugrasena and the wondrous Rama, with Pradyumna and others, came forth on chariots to meet him'; v.17: 'pradyumnas carudesnas ca sambo jambavati-sutah.'

statements.claim: The foremost elephant led the procession, brahmins chanted blessings, hundreds of courtesans rode out in vehicles, and actors, dancers, bards and panegyrists filled the road
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.18-20: 'varnendram puraskrtya brahmanaih sa-sumangalaih / varamukhayas ca sataso yanair tad-darsanotsukah / nata-nartaka-gandharvah suta-magadha-vandinah.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered the bows, embraces, hand-touches, smiles and glances of relatives and citizens, and himself honored the elders, brahmins with wives and the aged
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.21-23: 'bhagavan... prahva-bhivadana-slesa-kara-sparsa-smiteksanaih / svayam ca gurubhir vipraih sa-daraih sthavirair api.'

statements.claim: The noble women of Dwaraka watched from the terraces along the royal road; his chest was the home of fortune, his face the drinking vessel of their eyes
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.24-26: 'raja-margam gate krsne dvarakayah kula-striyah / sriyo nivaso yasyorah pana-patram mukham drsam.'

statements.claim: He passed beneath the white umbrella and waving fans, showered with flowers, to his father's house, where his mothers led by Devaki lifted him onto their laps
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.27-29: 'sitatapatra-vyajanair upaskrtah prasuna-varsair abhivarsitah pathi / pravisyas tu grham pitroh parisvaktah sva-matrbhih / tah putram ankam aropya sneha-snuta-payodharah.'

statements.claim: Then he entered his own palace fulfilling every desire; his wives, seeing their husband home after his long absence, embraced him with their children, and even to those who saw him constantly his two feet were always new
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.30-33: 'athavisat sva-bhavanam sarva-kamam anuttamam / patnyah patim prosya grhan-upagatam vilokya sanjata-mano-mahotsavah / ... yady apy asau parsva-gato raho-gatas tathapi tasyanghri-yugam navam navam.'

notes: Very close rendering of SB 1.11.1-33. Only loose spots are devotional paraphrase ('mother, friend, husband, father' list matches v.6) and generic crowd color ('rose and ran', joy 'like a tide'), which the passage supports in substance.

statements.claim: Arjuna came to Dwaraka, found the bodies of Krishna and Balarama and performed the obsequial rites for them and the rest of the slain
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (Wilson, pack): 'ARJUNA having found the bodies of Krishna and of Rama, performed for them, and the rest of the slain, the obsequial rites.'

statements.claim: The eight queens of Krishna, Rukmini at their head, embraced his body and entered the funeral fire; Revati, embracing Rama's corpse, entered the blazing pile, which was cool to her
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'The eight queens of Krishna... with Rukmini at their head, embraced the body of Hari, and entered the funeral fire. Revati also, embracing the corpse of Rama, entered the blazing pile, which was cool to her, happy in contact with her lord.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena and Vasudeva, with Devaki and Rohini, hearing this, committed themselves to the flames, and Arjuna performed their rites too
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Hearing these events, Ugrasena and Anakadundubhi, with Devaki and Rohini, committed themselves to the flames. The last ceremonies were performed for all these by Arjuna.'

statements.claim: Arjuna took Vajra and led the thousands of Krishna's wives and all the people from Dwaraka with tenderness and care
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'The son of Kunti conducted the thousands of the wives of Krishna, with Vajra, and all the people, from Dwaraka, with tenderness and care, and travelled slowly away.'

statements.claim: The Sudharman palace and the Parijata tree, brought down to earth by Krishna, went back to heaven; on the day Hari left the earth the dark Kali age descended
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'The Sudharman palace and the Parijata tree, which had been brought to earth by Krishna, both proceeded to heaven; and on the same day that Hari departed from the earth the powerful dark-bodied Kali age descended.'

statements.claim: The ocean rose and submerged Dwaraka except one temple of the Yadu deity, never washed away, where Kesava abides and visitors are freed from sins
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'The ocean rose, and submerged the whole of Dwaraka, except alone the dwelling of the deity of the race of Yadu... there Kesava constantly abides... Whoever visits that holy shrine... is liberated from all his sins.'

statements.claim: Arjuna halted the people in the Panchanada country, a rich and fertile spot, and robbers gathered the lawless Abhiras against the single warrior guarding widowed women and great riches
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Arjuna halted the people... in the Panchanada country, in a rich and fertile spot; but the desires of the robbers... were excited, when they observed so many widowed females... in the possession of Arjuna alone. Inflamed by their cupidity, they assembled the villainous Abhiras.'

statements.claim: The robbers mocked Arjuna as rich and proud of slaying Bhishma, Drona and Karna, ignorant of villagers' prowess, and rushed on the people with cudgels and clods of earth
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Here is this Arjuna, immensely rich... His pride is raised by the death of Bhishma, Drona, Jayadratha, Karna, and others... he does not know the prowess of simple villagers. Up, up; take your long thick staves... they rushed, armed with cudgels and clods of earth, upon the people.'

statements.claim: Arjuna told them to retire unless they wished to die; they ignored him and seized the treasure and the women
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Arjuna encountered them, and said to them in derision, Retire, wretches, ignorant of what is right, unless ye are desirous of dying. But they disregarded his menaces, and seized his treasures and his women.'

statements.claim: Gandiva would not brace, the string stayed slack, the incantations of the superhuman weapons would not return, the shafts merely scratched skin, even the arrows given by Agni were destroyed, and the barbarians carried off the women of the Vrishni and Andhaka tribes
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Arjuna began to brace his heavenly bow Gandiva... but it was in vain; for... it continued flaccid: neither could he call to recollection the incantations of the superhuman weapons... those shot from Gandiva merely scratched the skin. The arrows given him by Agni... now were themselves destroyed... he beat the banditti with the horn of his bow; but they only laughed... and the barbarians, in the sight of Arjuna, carried off all the women of the Vrishni and Andhaka tribes.'

statements.claim: Arjuna lamented 'Alas! I am deserted by my lord!' and in that instant Gandiva, the heavenly weapons, his chariot and horses perished before his eyes; he declared himself overcome by peasants without that righteous aid
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Alas! alas! I am deserted by my lord!... and in that instant the bow and heavenly arms, his car and steeds, perished entirely... These two arms are mine; mine is this fist... I am Arjuna: but without that righteous aid all these are pithless... without him I am overcome by peasants.'

statements.claim: Arjuna went to Mathura, installed the Yadava prince Vajra as its king, and there in a wood found Vyasa and prostrated himself at his feet
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Arjuna went to the city of Mathura, and there installed the Yadava prince, Vajra, as its king. There he beheld Vyasa, who was living in a wood... saluted him respectfully.'

statements.claim: Vyasa asked how Arjuna was shorn of his lustre and whether he had been beaten by his inferiors in battle
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'How is it that I see you thus shorn of your lustre?... Or, what is, most probably, the case, have you been beaten by your inferiors in battle?'

statements.claim: Arjuna sighed deeply and told him that Hari who was their strength and brightness had left them; Gandiva famed through the three worlds was foiled by peasants' sticks and Krishna's households carried off; it was a wonder that he lived
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (verified against full Wilson text, pack passage truncated here): 'Arjuna, having sighed deeply, related to Vyasa all the circumstances... Hari, who was our strength, our might... has left us... The bow Gandiva, that was famed throughout the three worlds, has been foiled... by the sticks of peasants... the whole households of Krishna... carried away by peasants... it is wonderful that I live.'

statements.claim: Vyasa told him to think no more of his disgrace, that time subjects all beings to similar vicissitudes, and that rivers, seas, mountains, gods, men, trees and insects are all created and destroyed by time
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack excerpt + full text): 'Think no more, my son, of your disgrace... Know that time subjects all beings to similar vicissitude... Rivers, seas, mountains, the whole earth, gods, men, animals, trees, insects are, all, created, and, all, will be destroyed, by time.'

statements.claim: Krishna came down to lift the earth's burden; that object is accomplished - all the kings are slain, the Vrishni race destroyed, nothing remained for him to do, so the lord departed with his ends fulfilled; at creation he creates, in duration preserves, at the end destroys
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (full text): 'These mighty works of Krishna... have been performed to relieve earth of its burthens: for this he has come down... This object has been, now, accomplished. All the kings (of the earth) are slain; the race of Vrishni and Andhaka is destroyed: no more remained for him to accomplish. Therefore has the lord departed... his ends being, all, fulfilled... At the period of creation, the god of gods creates; in that of duration, he preserves; and, at the end (of all), he is mighty to annihilate.'

statements.claim: Arjuna's defeat by miserable thieves was as much time's work as his victories; it is only the sport of the universal Hari
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (full text): 'In like manner as, through thy devotion to Vishnu, these were overthrown by thee, so, at last, has thy defeat by miserable thieves been wrought by time... Be assured, son of Pritha, that it is (but) the sport of the universal Hari.'

statements.claim: Ashtavakra story: a brahman crooked in eight places stood in water meditating for years; after the Asuras were overthrown the nymphs passed to a festival on Meru, praised him, and at his offer some asked for the best of men and sovereign of the Brahmans as husband; when he rose from the water they laughed at his crookedness and he cursed them to fall into the hands of thieves after obtaining the first of males, later softening that they would return to the sphere of the gods
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (full text): 'a Brahman, named Ashtavakra, was pursuing his religious penances, standing in water... for many years. In consequence of the overthrow of the Asuras, there was a great festival on the summit of Meru... they praised and hymned him... Whatever you wish for, ask of me... grant us a husband, the best of men, and sovereign of the Brahmans. So be it, replied Ashtavakra, and, thereupon, came up from the waters. When the nymphs beheld him... crooked in eight places, they could not restrain their merriment, but laughed aloud... you shall obtain the first of males for your husband; but... you shall (afterwards) fall into the hands of thieves... they should finally return to the sphere of the gods.'

statements.claim: It is because of that curse that the wives of Kesava have fallen into the hands of the barbarians; all this destruction was effected by the lord of all and Arjuna's end too is near, since he has withdrawn his strength and splendour
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (full text): 'It is in consequence, then, of the curse of the Muni Ashtavakra, that these females, who were, at first, the wives of Kesava, have, now, fallen into the hands of the barbarians... All this destruction has been effected by the lord of all; and your end is, also, nigh at hand, since he has withdrawn from you strength, splendour, valour, and preeminence.'

statements.claim: Death is the doom of everyone born, fall the end of exaltation, union terminates in separation, growth tends to decay; knowing this, wise men feel neither grief nor joy
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (full text): 'Death is the doom of every one who is born; fall is the end of exaltation; union terminates in separation; and growth tends but to decay. Knowing (all this), wise men are susceptible of neither grief nor joy.'

statements.claim: Vyasa told him to relinquish everything and repair to the holy forest, and to tell Yudhishthira that tomorrow, with his brothers, he must tread the path of heroes; Arjuna went back and told his brothers, and the sons of Pandu placed Parikshit on the throne and went to the forest
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (full text + pack excerpt): 'along with your brothers, relinquish everything, and repair to the holy forest. Go, now, and say, from me, to Yudhishthira, that he, to-morrow, with his brethren, tread the path of heroes... Thus instructed by Vyasa, Arjuna went and related to the other sons of Pritha all that he had seen... the sons of Pandu placed Parikshit on the throne, and went to the forest.'

notes: Pack passage truncates mid-dialogue (~'...or of the deat[h]'), so the second half (Vyasa's consolation, Ashtavakra tale, enthronement) was verified against the full Wilson VP 5.38 text that the pack cites; story tracks it almost verbatim. 'Arjuna went alone' is connective framing - VP has Daruka conduct Arjuna to Dwaraka and the text later stresses the wealth/women were 'in the possession of Arjuna alone.'
